definition: A model in which only a subset of parameters or pathways are active for any given input, in contrast to a dense model where all parameters participate in every computation.
details: Sparse architectures, such as mixture-of-experts models, allow scaling total parameter count without proportionally increasing the compute required per input.

explainer.lead: In a sparse model only a subset of parameters or pathways is active for any given input, unlike a dense model where all parameters participate in every computation. It matters because sparse architectures such as mixture-of-experts scale total parameter count without proportionally raising compute per input.

tiers.eli5: It is a huge team where only the few relevant specialists are called in for each job, rather than everyone working on every task.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use routing so each input activates only some experts, gaining capacity at lower per-input compute. The pitfall is uneven expert load, leaving some experts undertrained.
tiers.paperLevel: A model in which only a subset of parameters or pathways are active per input, contrasted with dense models where all parameters participate in every computation.

explainer.example: A mixture-of-experts layer routes each token to two of many expert subnetworks, so total parameters are large but compute per token stays small.
